summary:
Developed by us, Team Failed API call (which was originally meant to be Triple T), Mission: Architecture is an interactive space mission simulation game where the player builds, designs, and calculates according to their needs.
   Mission: Architecture is a retro-terminal-style space mission simulator featuring multi-planet missions, where players custom-build spacecraft, select scientific instruments, choose launch vehicles, and manage critical operational constraints.
   Through the gameplay, the player gets to make decisions on trade-offs which changes the tangible mission success rate. The player msut balance the budget, mass limit, power margins, communication links and immediately sees how every decision shapes the result. 
   Mission: Architecture Empowers students and space enthuisiasts the complete process of a space mission from the square one to the final scene.
details: The player steps into a retro-terminal-based simulation game where he or she designs spacecraft for different launch missions, balancing budgets, mass, and power to test their mission success rate via a Monte Carlo simulation. Mission: Architecture turns complex space engineering into hands-on, meaningful choices. Through trial and error, players build real problem-solving skills, experience what it truly takes to run a space mission from start to finish, and get inspired to explore what’s possible beyond Earth. While coding the game, Unity 6 (2D URP), C#, Unity New Input System, TextMeshPro, and custom pixel-art assets were used. Our project blends realistic physics and NASA data with a pixel-style CRT terminal aesthetic, creating a dynamic risk simulation experience. We considered the balance between realistic physics and playability, the interdependencies among components (mass, power, budget), and user experience.
